data.narrative:
Hyperscale Power is a seed-stage climate and energy company founded by Daniel Rothmund (PhD ETH Zurich, ex-ABB) and Sami Pettersson (ex-ABB), having raised €5M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Lonza, LNZA), though the peer set lacks sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private companies with directly comparable valuation profiles to support median-based triangulation.

Given data constraints, stage-progression analysis is the applicable method. Using total capital raised (€5M) as a value proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier from Seed to next stage yields an implied valuation of $12M. This multiplier reflects observed progression patterns within early-stage frontier-tech companies, though it carries inherent variance across market conditions and cohorts.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $11M–$14M (median $12M), derived from a single methodological anchor. Key uncertainties include: the representativeness of a 2.5x step-up multiplier for this founders' pedigree and sector; absence of near-peer data to validate or adjust the multiplier; and market-stage dynamics in climate-tech fundraising. Tightening this range would require either identifiable seed-stage peers in deep tech energy or clarity on the company's pathway to Series A metrics.
